questions.question: Q1: When operating the simulation dashboard in Manual Mode, what action allows you to change the total vehicle mass from 1500 kg to 2000 kg?

answers.a: Adjusting the surface friction coefficient dropdown menu options
answers.b: Dragging all four load blocks (Driver, Passengers, Suitcase, Crate) into the cargo hold zone
answers.c: Maximizing both the Front (P1) and Rear (P2) motor target sliders to 150 kW
answers.d: Switching the system views from Phase 1 into the Phase 2 mathematical proofs page

explanations.a: Incorrect. The friction dropdown changes road traction conditions ($\mu$) but does not modify physical mass metrics.
explanations.b: Correct. Dropping the Driver (80kg), Passengers (150kg), Suitcase (30kg), and Crate (240kg) aggregates 500kg of extra cargo, moving total mass to 2000kg.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Changing power parameters adjusts longitudinal load distribution calculations but does not change static mass parameters.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Toggling view windows displays the math data breakdown but does not structurally add weight variables into the active car model.

questions.question: Q2: What visual indication represents that an axle's traction capacity has been breached on the telemetry vector canvas?

answers.a: The forward green power arrow vanishes completely from the interface
answers.b: The battery flow cable animations reverse direction and move toward the center pack
answers.c: The parallel backward resistance vector arrow turns red, and a 'SLIP' text warning displays
answers.d: The steering rack tie-rods turn neon yellow and pulse continuously

explanations.a: Incorrect. The green arrow remains visible to illustrate the magnitude of power applied to the wheel.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The high-voltage cable animations follow spinning speed trends but do not physically invert direction path orientations.
explanations.c: Correct. When power exceeds grip limits, the resistance arrow switches color from grey to red, alongside canvas labels indicating SLIP.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The steering components are static vector elements that do not dynamically color-flash to signal traction issues.

questions.question: Q3: If you observe the vehicle simulation road animation stop moving while the wheels continue to spin, what scenario is being demonstrated?

answers.a: Optimal traction parameters across both vehicle axles
answers.b: Double axle slippage where both motors exceed local grip thresholds simultaneously
answers.c: The autonomous torque vectoring engine rerouting excess power from front to back
answers.d: A physical shutdown triggered by high thermal runaway conditions inside the cells

explanations.a: Incorrect. Under optimal traction conditions, the road moves at a speed proportional to the applied electrical output.
explanations.b: Correct. When both axles experience slip, the vehicle road backdrop animation pauses while the wheels spin continuously.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The autonomous control logic regulates active motor levels to ensure road travel animations match output parameters safely.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Thermal runaway is not modeled within the mechanical limits of this vehicle traction visualization dashboard.

questions.question: Q4: What is the systematic penalty applied to System Energy Efficiency if the front wheels experience traction slip while the rear wheels remain safe?

answers.c: The total system efficiency falls immediately to its minimum constraint of 10%
answers.d: No numeric penalty is incurred unless both axles break friction limits simultaneously

explanations.a: Incorrect. A 5% scale adjustment represents the base load loss calculation component, not the structural wheel slip penalty parameter.
explanations.b: Correct. The simulation logic applies a flat 20% penalty reduction to overall efficiency for each individual axle breaking traction.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The system efficiency lands at the 10% lower floor boundary only if double axle slip issues occur under heavy manual loads.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Any single axle breaking grip automatically triggers efficiency drops within the telemetry module.

questions.question: Q5: How do the target motor controls respond on the dashboard interface when Autonomous Torque Allocation is checked?

answers.a: The P1 and P2 sliders lock completely, display an 'Auto Active' badge, and grey out manual targets
answers.b: The input options disappear from the left sidebar and relocate inside the cargo trunk slots
answers.c: The sliders alternate colors rapidly to signal real-time driver input requests
answers.d: The input bounds scale up automatically from 150 kW limits to 300 kW peak values

explanations.a: Correct. Enabling autonomous mode disables manual input controls, sets a green badge notification, and automatically computes optimal power mapping.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The control box components stay fixed in the left sidebar menu area throughout the entire lab activity.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Color transitions are applied to status banners and warning labels, not interactive slider toggles.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The limits of the manual input components remain locked at 10 kW min and 150 kW max allocations.

questions.question: Q6: While using Manual Mode, what happens to the status warning banner if you slide the Front Motor Target to 120 kW while driving on Ice Road ($\mu = 0.2$)?

answers.a: It highlights in green stating 'OPTIMAL TRACTION'
answers.b: It turns yellow showing an 'AXLE SLIPPAGE DETECTED' warning label for the FRONT axle
answers.c: It turns red displaying a 'DOUBLE AXLE SLIPPAGE' critical message profile
answers.d: It hides completely behind the dynamic vector graphics canvas viewport layer

explanations.a: Incorrect. High power targets on ice surfaces cause calculations to breach grip limits, eliminating optimal green display statuses.
explanations.b: Correct. High inputs on a low friction surface (0.2) push power past front traction constraints, highlighting a yellow warning layout.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The message registers as a double axle warning only if the rear motor target also breaches its grip limits simultaneously.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The banner remains fully visible in the right panel to present critical safety diagnostic details.

questions.question: Q7: Which component is hidden from view inside the EV trunk visualization layout if you drop weight blocks inside it?

answers.a: The high-voltage orange cable networks tracking to the axles
answers.b: The text tags showing the specific name labels of the cargo items (e.g., 'Driver', 'Passengers')
answers.c: The brake calipers and rotor structural graphics details
answers.d: The telemetry readout indicators tracking overall motor kilowatt values

explanations.a: Incorrect. The high-voltage wiring lines remain visible around the layout frame structure.
explanations.b: Correct. To accommodate tight constraints inside the vehicle model chassis trunk space, the text labels drop out, leaving only icons and weights.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The red brake calipers and grey disc rotors remain anchored onto the wheel components.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Kilowatt metrics update continuously below the motor blocks, independent of cargo positions.

questions.question: Q8: How can you remove a load block from the vehicle cargo hold to return it back to the shelf storage section?

answers.a: Switching the interface layout into Phase 2 mode and back into Phase 1 mode
answers.b: Hovering over the block inside the trunk slots until the text displays 'REMOVE' and clicking it
answers.c: Dragging the surface friction condition dropdown select menu back to Dry Asphalt
answers.d: De-selecting the autonomous traction checkbox item on the control panel dashboard

explanations.a: Incorrect. Toggling view windows maintains current cargo loads and does not clear vehicle load states.
explanations.b: Correct. The layout features an interactive toggle action where hovering shows a clear option, and clicking returns the asset to the shelf.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Adjusting environment properties shifts calculated grip boundaries but does not clear active load elements.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Toggling the automation checkbox affects motor control logic but does not alter physical cargo assignments.

questions.question: Q9: What information does the 'Phase 2: Physics Proof' workspace display to validate calculations?

answers.a: A breakdown tracking inferred variables such as dynamic axle masses, road grip limits, and mathematical explanations
answers.b: A script command console window to manually update source code configuration parameters
answers.c: An interactive chart plotting historical tire wear attributes over extensive timelines
answers.d: A settings dashboard allowing engineers to modify chassis wheel lengths and axle configurations

explanations.a: Correct. Phase 2 breaks down active variables into real-time metrics, providing mathematical validation of traction conditions.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The verification panel displays pre-calculated metrics and statements, not a code terminal.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Long-term wear traits are outside the parameters monitored by the telemetry validation module.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The baseline architectural properties of the vehicle model are static parameters that cannot be configured by users.

questions.question: Q10: How does the road animation speed change when total power demand rises under optimal, non-slipping traction conditions?

answers.a: The animation velocity drops linearly, shifting toward a complete halt layout state
answers.b: The animation duration decreases, causing the background to move faster to reflect vehicle acceleration
answers.c: The backdrop switches instantly from standard asphalt stripes into solid neon colored lines
answers.d: The animation locks at a uniform 3.0s interval, independent of system power adjustments

explanations.a: Incorrect. The road animation slows down or pauses only when tires lose friction cohesion and slip.
explanations.b: Correct. The system translates higher stable power outputs into faster road movement by reducing the animation duration loop timer.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The visual markers are fixed based on the chosen road condition type and do not change with speed changes.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The uniform 3.0s setting is an instruction explicitly reserved for partial axle slippage warning periods.
